meta.phaseDetail: Magic 7-8, eighth in the East, 3-0 in NBA Cup group play. At Washington tonight, 7:00 PM; Cup group finale vs Detroit Tuesday.

brief.headline: Magic at Wizards tonight as 5.5-point favorites; injury list unchanged
brief.summary: Orlando (7-8) plays at Washington (6-11) at 7:00 PM on TV27 after a day off Saturday. The Magic are 5.5-point road favorites and are again without Banchero, Isaac, Penda and Nelson. Washington won the first meeting 103-94 in Orlando on Nov 2. A win would get the Magic back to .500 before Tuesday's NBA Cup group finale against Detroit, where a win clinches a quarterfinal spot.

bullets.text: Tonight at Washington, 7:00 PM, TV27 and DAZN. The Wizards have won two straight on the road (103-99 at Toronto, 98-94 at Chicago) and held Orlando to 94 points in the Nov 2 meeting (Covers).
Orlando -5.5, total 221.5 (market consensus via Dimers, 4:02 AM ET). Moneyline Magic -194 at Novig.

Banchero (ankle), Isaac (knee), Penda (hamstring) and Nelson (ankle) are out again (96.9 The Game). Washington is without Jamir Watkins (torn ACL), Reece Beekman (shoulder), Tristan Vukcevic (hip) and Justin Champagnie (foot).

Saturday: Philadelphia beat Milwaukee to reach 14-3, New York won its fourth straight and Boston lost its third in a row. Orlando stays eighth, 1 game behind seventh-place Cleveland and 2 behind sixth-place Miami (ESPN).
Orlando is 3-0 in East Group A and 14-4 all-time in Cup play. A win over Detroit at Kia Center on Tuesday clinches a Cup quarterfinal spot (Orlando Sentinel).
The Magic are 5-5 in clutch games. Sweeney said players have been offering ideas on late-game execution and he wants to keep "building those fundamentals, building those habits" (Orlando Sentinel).

preview.title: Sunday at Wizards, 7:00 PM, TV27
preview.text: Washington (6-11, 2-5 at home) has won two straight behind Anthony Davis and No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa, with Trae Young at point guard. The Wizards won 103-94 in Orlando on Nov 2. Banchero, Isaac, Penda and Nelson are out for Orlando; Wagner is averaging 25.1 points and 8.4 assists.

players.name: Paolo Banchero
players.note: Team leader in points and rebounds last season. Spent the summer working out with Kevin Durant.
players.statusNote: Ruled out Sunday at Washington, his 14th straight missed game. Said Nov 19 he does not know when he will return but hopes it is "within the next couple of weeks"; he has done some on-court work, mostly shooting, and wants the ankle fully healed before coming back (Orlando Sentinel). Sweeney said Nov 18 there is no timeline.

players.name: Franz Wagner
players.note: Missed 48 games last season with a high ankle sprain, then strained his right calf in the playoffs. Left the preseason finale with right shoulder soreness but practiced fully Oct 20 and is off the injury report. Career-high 15 assists Nov 5 at Phoenix, with 6 turnovers. Tied his career high with 38 points Nov 11 at Utah, his third straight 30-point game. Scored 27 with 11 assists Nov 18 vs Philadelphia, his sixth straight 20-point game. Scored 35 with the game-winning jumper with 2.4 seconds left Nov 20 at Brooklyn, his fifth 30-point game this season.

players.name: Desmond Bane
players.note: Played all 82 games last season. Missed Nov 7 at Golden State with an illness, his first missed game with Orlando. Made 7 of 11 threes for 25 points Nov 11 at Utah. Set a team record Nov 18 vs Philadelphia with his ninth straight game of three or more threes, passing Rashard Lewis, and extended it to 10 games Nov 20 at Brooklyn with 7 of 13 threes.

players.name: Jalen Suggs
players.note: Led the team in assists and steals last season. Missed eight games with a right knee bone bruise (Oct 25), returned off the bench Nov 13 and was back in the starting lineup Nov 16 at Boston. Minutes are being managed.

players.contract: $10.1M. Final rookie-scale year. No extension; restricted free agent in 2027
players.name: Anthony Black
players.note: No rookie-scale extension by the Oct 19 deadline; restricted free agent in 2027. Sat out Nov 2 vs Washington to manage a right ankle sprain and returned Nov 5 at Phoenix. Left Nov 7 at Golden State with a cramp with 2:47 left in overtime and did not return, per Sweeney.

players.name: Wendell Carter Jr.
players.note: Competing with Vucevic for the starting center spot. Had 27 points and 13 rebounds on 10-of-12 shooting Nov 5 at Phoenix.

players.name: Nikola Vucevic
players.note: Back in Orlando after playing here from 2012 to 2021. Split last season between Chicago and Boston. Had his best game of the season Nov 20 at Brooklyn: 15 pts on 5-of-5 shooting (3-of-3 from three) and 8 rebounds in 23 minutes.

players.contract: $4.0M. 2027-28 team option ($6.1M) exercised Oct 21; signed through 2027-28
players.name: Tristan da Silva
players.note: Played World Cup qualifiers for Germany in August. Moved to the bench Nov 16 when Suggs rejoined the starting lineup.

players.name: Goga Bitadze
players.note: Scored 23 for Georgia in an Aug 28 World Cup qualifier. Projects as the third center.

players.name: Jonathan Isaac
players.note: Waived June 27 and re-signed on a minimum deal July 1.
players.statusNote: Ruled out Sunday at Washington (left knee injury management). RotoWire calls him week-to-week until Orlando gives a clear return update. Assigned to Osceola and recalled Nov 1, presumably for practice. Told the Orlando Sentinel (Oct 28) he expects to play this season. Has not played since March 12.

players.name: Jevon Carter
players.note: Re-signed July 1. Stats shown are his 30 games with Orlando.

players.name: Jamal Cain

players.contract: $3.1M rookie scale. 2027-28 team option ($3.3M) exercised Oct 21
players.name: Jase Richardson
players.note: Averaged 18.3 points in Summer League. Made his first NBA start Oct 25 at New York in place of Banchero.

players.name: Noah Penda
players.note: Seen as the long-term defensive forward off the bench. Returned from a right hamstring strain Oct 11 (8 pts, 5 reb, 5 ast).
players.statusNote: Ruled out Sunday at Washington. Said Nov 14 he is running but not yet doing full-speed sprints; Sweeney said he is "progressing well and ramping up" and is evaluated weekly. No timetable.

players.name: Alex Morales
players.note: Made his first NBA start Nov 11 at Utah (5 pts, 4 reb, 3 ast in 17 min). Set career highs of 7 points and 7 rebounds the night before at Sacramento.

players.name: Izaiyah Nelson
players.note: AAC Player of the Year at South Florida: 15.9 points, 9.6 rebounds.
players.statusNote: Ruled out Sunday at Washington. Sweeney said Nov 18 he is "progressing, doing some on-court stuff here, a little bit at a time," but the work is "just minimal"; no timeline (Jason Beede, Orlando Sentinel). Had surgery this offseason on the left ankle he fractured in Summer League and has not made his NBA debut.

22nd, up from 23rd (net rating -4.8). Says Wagner "is starting to look more capable of carrying an offense like an alpha," while noting the wins came against two of the league's weakest teams.

23rd, down from 22nd (net rating -8.9). Gives Orlando "a bit of a pass" for Banchero's absence but says it is "probably past time to worry" and that the Banchero-Wagner pairing "has never totally worked."
20th after one week, down from 16th. Notes Orlando was headed to its third starting lineup in four games.
20th, down four spots. Says the win at New York without Banchero shows Orlando can still be feisty in his absence.
19th. Says this team cannot stay healthy and may be in too big a hole to fight for more than a Play-In berth.
16th in Week 2, down from 15th. Net rating 19th at -5.4; notes the league's biggest jump in 3-point rate.
15th, up one. Says the injuries raise major questions about the future of this core.
11th of 15 in its East opening-week rankings after the opening loss to Atlanta, calling it concerning for a team with high expectations.
15th to start the season. Sees a range from the East's top four to 9th-10th; says restoring the defense should be Sweeney's primary task.
Leans Over 43.5 wins but says he would stay away from the bet. Better health could mean 48-50 wins; the team could also slip into the 30s.
15th overall. Calls it a borderline make-or-break season for the Banchero-Wagner pairing.
19th overall, 11th in the East. Cites 3-point shooting.

staffChanges: Jamahl Mosley fired May 4 after five seasons (189-221). Now head coach of the Pelicans.
God Shammgod, Bret Brielmaier, Dale Osbourne and Randy Gregory followed Mosley to New Orleans.
Assistant GM Stephen Mervis left for the Bulls on May 14.

transactions.text: Assigned Jonathan Isaac to the Osceola Magic and recalled him the same day, presumably to practice with the affiliate (RotoWire).
Exercised 2027-28 rookie-scale team options on Tristan da Silva (about $6.1M) and Jase Richardson (about $3.3M).
Anthony Black's rookie-scale extension deadline passed with no agreement; he will be a restricted free agent in 2027.
Waived Malaki Branham, JD Davison and Kevin Knox II after the preseason finale.
Signed Kevin Knox II to an Exhibit 10 deal. Unlike the four players signed and waived Sept 22, Knox stays in training camp; roster now stands at 20.
Signed Ace Baldwin Jr., Ricky Council IV, Jarron Cumberland and Au'Diese Toney to Exhibit 10 deals and waived all four the same day to secure their G League rights for Osceola.
Signed Malaki Branham and JD Davison to Exhibit 10 camp deals.
Re-signed Jevon Carter and Jonathan Isaac (1 yr, minimum each).
Re-signed Colin Castleton and signed No. 51 pick Izaiyah Nelson to two-way deals.
Moritz Wagner left for Brooklyn (2 yrs, $19M). Jett Howard later signed a two-way with Dallas.
Waived Jonathan Isaac before his $14.5M salary guaranteed. $8M dead money this season.
Draft: traded No. 46 (Felix Okpara) to Washington for No. 51 (Izaiyah Nelson) and No. 60; sent No. 60 to Milwaukee for cash. No first-round pick (owed to Memphis from the Bane trade).
Hired Sean Sweeney as head coach.
